newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-BRITISH DRIVERS SWEEP FRONT ROW QUALIFYING.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BRITISH DRIVERS SWEEP FRONT ROW QUALIFYING.

text.p: Rookie Dario Franchitti on Saturday led a British sweep of front row qualifiers for Sunday's Toronto Grand Prix CART race in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Mark Blundell, a winner four weeks ago, was second at 58.926 seconds in another Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Bobby Rahal of the United States was third in a Reynard Ford at 59.050 seconds.

Franchitti, a 24-year-old born in Scotland, set a track record of 58.618 seconds at 105.694 mph (170.170 kph) around the 11-turn, 1.72 mile (2.77 km) road circuit. It was his first series' pole position in only his 11th race and the first front row sweep for British drivers in this series.

Driving for an unsponsored team owned by Carl Hogan, Franchitti's feat brought tears to his owner's eyes, and when he exited his racer the rookie just about disappeared in the arms of his owner's bear hug.
"It's good for the United Kingdom to show that we can compete in any international series," Franchitti said. "It means a lot to the guys back home."
Provisional pole winner Michael Andretti fell to fourth after blowing up his engine in the morning practice run.
Driving a Swift Ford, Andretti's best lap was 59.120 seconds.
"I really wanted to win the Toronto pole," he said. "Poles are sometimes tougher to win than the race."
Sunday's 95-lap race, for which 28 drivers have qualified, is the 11th in the 17-race series.
